The existing MODIFY captures the new terminal style but leaves a stale exclusivity attribute stating that the expressive terminal belongs only to the Hero V and É accent, whereas the source now applies the refined terminal consistently to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

After comparing the kerning studies together, I am definitely most attracted to Option 2 (Balanced Flow). It reads as one unified word but still retains the airiness and elegance we have been developing.

Before proceeding with the material treatments, I want to reconsider the terminal used by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

We devoted substantial time to perfecting the Hero V before the rest of the alphabet had been created. At that point, the Hero V had to express far more of the identity by itself. With the complete wordmark now assembled, I no longer think it needs to be so expressive or decorative.

I’m seeking a feeling of precision, assurance, and quiet elevation. I’d like to test a terminal that appears more deliberate and architectural—a restrained, controlled upward release instead of a flourish.

I’m attaching two references that start to convey the quality I mean. I do not want either one reproduced exactly, but their cleaner transitions and more restrained elevation appeal to me.

The established structure and slope of both the Hero V and second V should remain unchanged. Instead, please create a few interpretations that preserve that geometry while applying a consistently refined terminal to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

Thank you!

value_updates.terminal_style: Use the same deliberate, architectural, restrained, and controlled upward-release terminal as the Hero V rather than an expressive or decorative flourish.

decisions.reason: The source limits the terminal revision to the Hero V, second V, and É accent; the E and L remain governed by their existing restrained architectural design philosophy.
The existing message-189 MODIFY already fully replaces the prior kerning-study format with the requested comparative terminal interpretations and preservation constraints.
The existing message-189 MODIFY already records that structure, slope, hierarchy, and other established decisions remain locked while only the shared terminal treatment is varied.
Refining the shared terminal does not revoke or change the requirement that the É accent and Hero V peaks align on the same horizontal reference line.
The client expressly preserves the second V's established geometry while changing only its terminal, so its existing height hierarchy remains unchanged.
The message independently selects Option 2 Balanced Flow, which is already represented by the existing message-189 MODIFY; the terminal revision does not alter that kerning selection.
The terminal study occurs before proceeding with material treatments but does not change the selected Satin Reflection champagne-gold finish or its desired character.
Changing the shape of the shared terminal does not change which wordmark elements receive champagne gold or which elements remain black.
The terminal refinement preserves the established letter geometry and does not alter the shared-baseline requirement.
The source changes terminal styling only and does not reconsider the all-caps wordmark treatment.
